result.topic_en: Calculations on Riemann invariants for one-dimensional isentropic gas flow: characteristic equations for the invariants p and q, the change of independent variables to characteristic coordinates m and n, and the resulting linear second-order equation with its Jacobian Δ.
result.transcription:
$dp' = \frac{dp'}{dr}(dr - (u+a)dt) + \frac{2aa}{r}dt$
$dq' = \frac{dq'}{dr}(dr - (u-a)dt) + \frac{2aa}{r}dt$
$dr - (u+a)dt = \mu\, dn$ \quad $d(r-(u+a)t) + t\,du$
$dr - (u-a)dt = \nu\, dm$
$2a\,dt = \nu\, dm - \mu\, dn$
$2a\,dr = (u+a)\nu\, dm - (u-a)\mu\, dn$
$\frac{dp}{dn} = \frac{2aa}{r}\frac{dt}{dn} = \frac{1}{u+a}2aa\cdot\frac{\partial \log r}{\partial n}$
$\frac{dq}{dm} = \frac{2aa}{r}\frac{dt}{dm} = \frac{1}{u-a}2aa\frac{\partial \log r}{\partial m}$

$p = f(m) \quad q = \varphi(n)$
$\partial \log r = \frac{1}{2aa}\int (u-a)\,dq$
$r = e^{\frac{1}{2aa}\int(u-a)dq}$
$t = \frac{1}{2aa}\int e^{\frac{1}{2aa}\int(u-a)dq}\,dq$

[-$(u-a)\frac{\partial q}{\partial \log r} = 2aa$-] \quad $u = \frac{r}{t} - 2a\frac{dt}{dm}$
[-$\frac{\partial q}{\partial \log r} = a$-]
$\frac{\partial m}{\partial t} = \frac{1}{-2a\frac{dt}{dm}}$ \quad $\frac{\partial m}{\partial t} = \frac{u+a}{2a\frac{\partial t}{\partial m}}$
[-$\frac{(u+a)}{2aa}$-] \quad $\frac{dp'}{dr}(dr - (u+a)dt) = \left(\frac{dp'}{dm} - \frac{dq'}{dm}\right)dm$

$\frac{dp'}{dn}dn + \frac{dp'}{dm}dm$
[-$dq = \frac{dq}{dm}dm +$-] \quad $= \frac{dp'}{dm}dm + \frac{2aa}{r}dt$
$- \frac{2aa}{r}\frac{dt}{dm}dm$
$\frac{\partial p}{\partial t} + (u+a)\frac{\partial p}{\partial r} = 2\frac{aa}{r}$
$\frac{\partial q}{\partial t} + (u-a)\frac{\partial q}{\partial r} = 2\frac{aa}{r}$

$\left(\frac{1}{\Delta}\left((u+a)\frac{\partial m}{\partial q}\frac{\partial n}{\partial q} + (u-a)\frac{\partial n}{\partial p}\frac{\partial m}{\partial q}\right)dq\right.$
$+ \frac{1}{\Delta}\left((u+a)\frac{\partial m}{\partial q}\frac{\partial n}{\partial p} + (u-a)\frac{\partial n}{\partial p}\frac{\partial m}{\partial p}\right)$

$dp = \frac{dp}{dn}dn + \frac{dp}{dm}dm$
$= \frac{2aa}{r}\frac{dt}{dn}dn + \frac{dp}{dm}dm - \frac{2aa}{r}\frac{dt}{dm}dm$

$\frac{1}{r}\left(\frac{\partial\, r\frac{dp}{dn}}{\partial m} - \frac{\partial\, r\frac{dq}{dm}}{\partial n}\right) = 0 = \frac{\partial^2 p}{\partial m\partial n} - \frac{\partial^2 q}{\partial m \partial n} + \frac{\partial p}{\partial n}\frac{\partial q}{\partial m}\left(\frac{u-a}{2aa} - \frac{u+a}{2aa}\right) = 0$
$\frac{\partial^2 p}{\partial m\partial n} - \frac{\partial^2 q}{\partial m\partial n} - \frac{1}{a}\frac{\partial p}{\partial n}\frac{\partial q}{\partial m} = 0$
$\frac{\partial (u+a)\frac{dp}{dn}}{\partial m} - \frac{\partial (u-a)\frac{dq}{dm}}{\partial n} = 0$

[-$dp = \frac{dp}{dn}dn + \frac{dp}{dm}dm$-]
[-$dq = $-]
$dn = \frac{\partial n}{\partial p}dp + \frac{\partial n}{\partial q}dq$
$dm = \frac{\partial m}{\partial p}dp + \frac{\partial m}{\partial q}dq$
$\Delta\, dp = \frac{\partial m}{\partial q}dn - \frac{\partial n}{\partial q}dm$
$\Delta\, dq = -\frac{\partial m}{\partial p}dn + \frac{\partial n}{\partial p}dm$

$p = f(m) \quad \frac{\partial^2 q}{\partial m\partial n} = 0$
$(u-a)\frac{\partial q}{\partial m} = \psi(m)$
$(u+a)\frac{dp}{dn}dn + (u-a)\frac{dq}{dm}dm$
$(u+a)\frac{dp}{dn}dn + (u-a)\frac{dq}{dm}dm = \cdot\cdot$ \quad [-...-] \quad $-2a\frac{\partial t}{\partial m}dm$
$= dr - (u+a)dt$
$\frac{1}{\Delta}\left((u+a)\frac{\partial m}{\partial q}dn + (u-a)\frac{\partial n}{\partial p}dm\right)$ \quad $\frac{\partial q}{\partial r} = \frac{\frac{\partial q}{\partial m}}{-2a\frac{\partial t}{\partial m}}$

[-$\partial q$-]
$\frac{\partial q}{\partial t} = (u+a)\frac{a}{r}$ \quad $\frac{\partial q}{\partial r} = -\frac{a}{r}$
$-\frac{a}{r}$

methods.what: Characteristic equations for Riemann invariants with geometric source term
Introduction of characteristic coordinates m, n
Expressing dt, dr in terms of characteristic differentials
Derivatives of invariants along characteristics via log r
Integration of r and t in the simple-wave case p=f(m), q=φ(n)
Compatibility (integrability) condition yielding second-order equation in characteristic coordinates
methods.quote: $\frac{\partial^2 p}{\partial m\partial n} - \frac{\partial^2 q}{\partial m\partial n} - \frac{1}{a}\frac{\partial p}{\partial n}\frac{\partial q}{\partial m} = 0$

methods.what: Inversion of variables (hodograph-type) with Jacobian Δ
Special case p=f(m) leading to q_{mn}=0
